CDF-AS1.name: Broad / discovery response
CDF-AS1.who: A broad, relatively cold audience is plausible. Low auction cost and weak click response support this reading.
CDF-AS1.implication: Test a clear product introduction against the strongest existing creative.
CDF-AS1.alternative: Cheap placements or weaker creative delivery could produce a similar profile.
evidence: 159 cleaned ad-day observations; pooled CTR 1.15%, CPM €5.21.
Median daily frequency per ad 1.031; this is not deduplicated audience reach.
Within-ad late/first-week CTR ratio, season-adjusted: 0.72 across 3 ads.
Same-asset/day relative CTR median 0.67; a descriptive matched comparison.
Black Friday creative CTR / all-creative CTR 0.91; creative/date mix confounds this comparison.
CDF-AS1.confidence: Moderate for relative behaviour; low for targeting identity; demographics unobserved.
CDF-AS1.demographics: Age, gender, income, geography and placement cannot be recovered from these aggregates.

CDF-AS2.name: Promotion-responsive prospecting hypothesis
CDF-AS2.who: An interest or lookalike prospecting audience is plausible. Promotion response should be tested rather than assumed.
CDF-AS2.implication: Compare promotion, scarcity and urgency on the same dates. Watch the measured creative fatigue.
CDF-AS2.alternative: Creative mix and launch dates can explain apparent deal sensitivity.

CDF-AS2.demographics: Age, gender, income, geography and placement cannot be recovered from these aggregates.

CDF-AS3.name: Mixed prospecting response / identity uncertain
CDF-AS3.who: An interest-based audience is plausible, but the observed signals do not reliably distinguish deal seekers from selective shoppers.

CDF-AS3.alternative: Creative mix, delivery and time effects can explain the differences between these ad sets.
